chunks: He said and Baqubaqa, the brother of Bani al-Sayrafi, narrated: Al-Istakhri said to me: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
As if I can see the son of Hamida upon its branches (or pillars), the east of the earth and the west of it have become submissive to him.

key_terms.أَعْوَادِهَا: Its branches or pillars, referring to the foundation or lineage of the Imamate
key_terms.ابْنُ حَمِيدَةَ: Son of Hamida, a title often associated with Imam Musa al-Kadhim or the Mahdi in Shia texts
key_terms.دَانَتْ لَهُ: Became submissive or obedient to him
key_terms.شَرْقُ الْأَرْضِ وَغَرْبُهَا: The east and west of the earth, symbolizing the entire world

ai.seo_question: What does the metaphor of the son of Hamida signify in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* utilizes the metaphor of the 'son of Hamida' to prophesy the eventual global dominion of the Imamate, specifically linking it to the lineage of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s). Historically, this serves as a key evidence against the *Waqifiya* (those who stopped believing in the Imamate after a specific Imam) by affirming the continuity of authority and the ultimate political and spiritual victory of the Ahl al-Bayt. The phrase 'east and west' underscores the universality of this rule, fulfilling the divine promise of inheritance upon the earth.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 43 - Baqubaqa, brother of Bani Sairafi said: Istakhri said: I heard Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) say:
As if I can see the son of Hamida; that he has occupied the position of Imamate and the whole world has humbled before him.
